title: Recording King Cotton with Slim and keeping a road book
summary: At a Specialty session with Bumps Blackwell he improvised King Cotton, got no credit, and kept a book of dates and pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Wow. Did, it seemed to be, when you played piano, I mean mostly you were sideman. You were a sideman.

I've always been a sideman. I made a, we made a recording out there with Bumps Blackwell with Slim. We was in the studio out there for specialty. And Bumps wanted me to play something funky over there, God. So I just came up with a little idea. And the day I recorded it I really wasn't into it, you know. I was just playing something funky on the piano, you know. And then later on he called it King Cotton. And on one side, on one side it had heavy sugar. But Bumps Blackwell he butchered that song up man. It really was beautiful the way the guy had arranged the thing for the band. We used to play it every night. It was a nice arrangement. But he played it as to what things were going on at the time. But it really didn't take off. King Cotton took off more than heavy sugar did. And they played on WWOZ one time. They called it heavy sugar. But it's not heavy sugar. That's King Cotton. They play it, you know.
But I never would get anything for it. I just.
You wrote it? You mean you wrote. I played it.
Oh okay. So it was just conceived in the studio.
Just conceived in the studio and that's all. That's all that happened to it.
So you were on a session with Slim.

On a session with Slim in Bumps Blackwell. He played something. He was trying to get an idea for Slim. He wanted to get something else for him to play. That's the thing about it. I've been on many sessions with Slim. But when this guy came, he said he was going to give his itinerary and the places where we recorded and the places we had gone, that's why I let him have the stuff. Otherwise I never would have let him take my stuff away from there.

No it wasn't a book because they didn't know I had a book. Nobody said. Wherever we went I kept up with my dates. So I make sure I get my right money when we played jobs. We played a pilot theater. We went there several times. We played the Howard Theater and we played all up and down the Chittlin Circus you know.
And that was the reason you kept the book?

Well I kept the book because I wanted to know where it was going and what kind of money I was getting. That was one way of keeping up with things. And I came back and I was looking at the book about a month ago man. I don't know what happened to it. I know it's in the house somewhere.
